title: Canary release checklist + notes (scratchpad) - isaac chen
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the next canary rollout (model-serving runtime + api route). Not the final playbook - working through sequence, checks, and pinning notes. Use this to drive the PR checklist and pair with the official canary playbook on Confluence.

High-level plan (target):
- Deploy model-serving v2.3.1 (inference-runtime image: rwd-infer:v2.3.1) to staging then canary in prod.
- Canary traffic ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% (manual gates, canary duration each step 15-30m depending on perf).
- Fall back policy: immediate rollback to v2.3.0 if latency P95 increase > 100ms or error rate > 0.5% for 5m window.

Pre-deploy (checklist):
- [ ] Confirm release branch and tag: release/v2.3.1 created, Docker image built and pushed (sha: abcdef123456). Link in PR.
- [ ] Verify infra (nodes & capacity): autoscale group health, GPU utilization baseline < 60% on current traffic.
- [ ] Confirm canary config exists in routing service (route: /api/generate -> split by weight). Create new route if missing.
- [ ] Verify monitoring dashboards are up-to-date: latency/throughput, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, KV-cache hit rate.
- [ ] Prepare smoke-test script (see below) and run against staging.
- [ ] Update version pin doc for downstream consumers (internal env vars, lambda layers).
- [ ] Slack channel for rollout: #prod-rollout + ping oncall SRE.

Staging smoke tests (must pass before prod):
- Run small-batch generation (10 requests) for short/med/long seq lengths: 32, 512, 2048. Validate outputs are returned within baseline latency +- 20% and no errors.
- Run token-generation stress: 1k concurrent requests (staging scale equivalent) to exercise autoscaling paths. Look for OOMs or degraded KV-cache behavior.
- Run deterministic eval prompts (from quality-monitoring promptset v2) and compare top-level metrics (perplexity, quality-check flags).

Canary rollout steps (manual gate at each):
1) Deploy canary: create deployment rwd-infer:v2.3.1 with weight 1% on route /api/generate.
   - kubectl apply -f canary-deployment-v2.3.1.yaml (or use infra pipeline).
   - Verify pod ready, image sha matches.
2) Wait 15m, monitor:
   - Latency: P50/P95/P99; compare to baseline (v2.3.0).
   - Errors: 5xx, 4xx increase, timeouts.
   - Throughput: tokens/sec, batch sizes.
   - Cost signals: token cost per-minute (for dedicated customers).
   - Business metrics: any alerts from client integrations (routing traces).
3) If metrics stable -> increase to 5% (15-30m). Repeat.
4) If stable -> 20% (30m). Run extended smoke-tests and run the full eval promptset.
5) If stable -> 50% (30-60m). Confirm autoscaling behavior under higher load.
6) If stable -> 100% cutover and mark release as done.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Any sustained P95 latency > baseline + 100ms for 5 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
- OOM or container restarts > 1 per pod in 10 minutes.
- Quality regression: automated eval metric drop > threshold (TBD per-model).

Rollback steps:
- Set route weight back to previous stable version (v2.3.0) immediately.
- Scale canary pods to 0 if necessary.
- Open incident on PagerDuty, tag release engineer and SRE.
- Capture logs (kubectl logs) and collect core dumps if present.

Version pinning notes (for clients & infra):
- Runtime image: rwd-infer:v2.3.1 (sha: abcdef123456) -> update in deployment configs and serverless env variables.
- Model weights pinned by hash in model-registry: model-english-1.4 sha: m12345 -> confirm consistent across staging/prod.
- If providing fallback variants, list compatible model variants and quantization levels.
- Document which APIs change (none expected) and backward compatibility checks passed.

Monitoring & dashboards to watch (links in Confluence playbook):
- api/generate latency dashboard (P50/P95/P99)
- error budget burn (5xx/timeouts)
- resource utilization (GPU mem, CPU, host network)
- KV-cache hit rate + eviction rate (small changes can alter perf)
- APM traces sampled for canary requests (ensure traces show expected operator calls)

Smoke-test script (quick):
- POST /api/generate with seed prompts: 
  - short: "Summarize: Redwood's mission"
  - mid: 512-token completion prompt (from promptset)
  - long: 2048-token continuation (timeout set to 180s)
- Validation: HTTP 200, no error codes, token count matches expectation, latency < baseline + 20%
- Run in parallel with 5 concurrent clients for each sequence length.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm exact thresholds for quality-regression alerts (coordinate with APPLIED-ML).
- [ ] Do we need a special rolling update for KV cache warmup? Might require traffic priming script.
- [ ] Check if dedupe-caching layer changes in v2.3.1 impact cold-start p95 - plan for prewarmed replica.
- [ ] Add a pre-canary synthetic job that primes top-50 prefixes overnight.

Post-release (after 24-48h):
- Run full evaluation suite and compare against baseline.
- Check cost per-token change; update Optimize recommendations if needed.
- Postmortem notes template if issues encountered.
- Update release notes for customers (changelog blurb).

Notes to self:
- Keep communications short & clear in #prod-rollout. Call immediate rollback if criteria met.
- Pair with Maya on the 20% -> 50% transition (she owns monitoring alerts).
- Save artifacts: kube manifests, canary metrics snapshots, smoke-test logs, PR link.

End of scratchpad.
